newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary starts Holocaust victims compensation.
newsitem.headline: Hungary starts Holocaust victims compensation.

text.p: Hungary took its first concrete step on Thursday towards compensating some 20,000 Hungarian Jew survivors of the Holocaust.
The cabinet -- pending parliament approval -- allocated four billion forints ($25 million) for special compensation coupons to be used to fund annuities for elderly survivors.
A Finance Ministry official said the annuities were just part of the planned compensation,
"The complete package will consist of compensation coupons, real estate, art works and cash," Laszlo Akar, state secreatry of the Finance Ministry, told Reuters.

Hungary's parliament approved a law in October creating a foundation to administer property confiscated from Hungarian Jews during World War Two and to oversee payments to survivors of the Nazi extermination campaign.
The government promised to set up the foundation in July after talks with the World Jewish Congress and other groups.
"The foundation will be set up as soon as parliament approves the proposed four billion compensation," Akar said.
Leaders of Hungary's Jewish community were not available for comment. One had told Reuters previously that four billion forints was a "first little step" and far from enough.
He called for further talks about who would be on the governing board of the foundation and what real estate the government would offer.
Akar said the 1997 budget proposal -- still under debate in parliament -- contains 30 million forints cash compensation to Holocaust survivors and there is more to come.
"There will be at least this amount set aside from the budget for the coming years," he said.
"Negotiations are continuing regarding real estate and art works," Akar said.
Hungary, before World War Two, had an estimated 800,000 to one million Jews, one of the wealthiest Jewish communities in Europe.
